purpose: What Microsoft Word shows for REF fields with the \r (relative context) switch, by where the field sits, so generated relative cross-references carry the same cached result (#1258).
procedure: Each probe `spec` was compiled with generateDocx (every cross-reference number: 'relative'; the probes were first written with \w and rewritten to \r, the same instruction). Word opened each DOCX bound by its name only, `update field` ran on every field of the document and of each footnote through AppleScript, and each field's code and result were read back; the document was closed by name without saving. The same DOCX was converted to PDF with headless LibreOffice and read with pdftotext. The `create` documents were built with `docx-markdoc create --require-pdf` from the recorded sources; every check passed. Their fields were updated in Word as above, and again after a Heading 2 paragraph was inserted and fields were updated.
finding: \r shows the \w (full context) number less the leading levels whose values the target shares with a position, always keeping the target's own level (its \n part, a trailing period dropped). The position is the last paragraph of the TARGET's list (w:numId) at or before the paragraph holding the field, not the field's own paragraph: an unnumbered paragraph or table cell after 2.03(c) shows (b) for 2.03(b); a field in a clause of the heading list shows (b) for a preface-list 2(b) whose list last numbered that 2(b); a field in a list of another definition, or of another w:num of the same definition, is not relative to its own list. With no paragraph of the target's list before the field, the full number is shown. A part that names level 0 (Section %1.%2) is kept whole: Section 2.03(b) from Section 2.04(a). A field in a footnote shows the full number wherever the footnote is anchored (none of the footnote stories holds a numbered paragraph). LibreOffice 26.2 agrees with Word on every field of probe1 (legal headings), and otherwise keeps the period before ( ('2.(b)') and is relative to the last paragraph of any w:num of the target's definition (probe2 b2a/c2a, probe3 y3/y3a), so it differs from Word when two w:num instances of one definition are used.
generation: generateDocx's cached results equal Word's after-update results for all 106 probe fields and for both created documents; create's cached results equal Word's after the Section insertions too (the markdocEquivalent source). create refuses a relative reference to an item of an ordered list outside numbered headings unless it sits before every such list or after its target's own list with no other such list starting in between (XREF_RELATIVE_ACROSS_LISTS), because there Word and LibreOffice disagree.

spec.text: Inserts the entire paragraph number of the bookmarked paragraph in relative context—or relative to its position in the numbering scheme—without trailing periods.
